newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-BOBEK TOO SHAKEN BY FASSI'S DEATH.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-BOBEK TOO SHAKEN BY FASSI'S DEATH.

text.p: Nicole Bobek tried her heart out but it just was not there for her in the final of the world figure skating championships on Saturday.
Just two days after the sudden death from a heart attack of her coach, Carlo Fassi, the memory of her mentor proved too much of a handicap to overcome as she dropped from eighth to 13th place.
The American skater knelt on the ice at the end of her performance to pay a brief silent tribute to the man who had guided her fortunes and restored her as a top-level skater.
"I just wanted Carlo to know I was thinking of him," she said.

Bobek, who worked with Fassi earlier in her tempestuous career, had returned to him last August after she missed the 1996 world championships because of injury and it seemed that she had found peace at last after switching coaches 10 times previously.
Bobek, 19, had taken the bronze medal in 1995 and came to Lausanne as a solid medal contender after a fine free-skating display lifted her to third place in the U.S. Nationals last month.
But with the weight of Thursday's tragedy on her shoulders, her performance was one she will want to forget.
She did not manage a clean triple jump, either scaling down her jumps or touching down with her hands on landing.
"I want to forget it all and I wish none of this had ever happened," she said later. "I wish there was a positive to take from this world championship but there is not.
"I just couldn't get my feet under me out there. I tried but it was just too hard," she said. "My mind was racing and I tried but I couldn't do it."
Bobek was accompanied before her performance by Fassi's widow Christa, his coaching partner, and by Briton Robin Cousins, the 1980 Olympic champion who was one of his pupils.
She cried as she left the ice and as she and Christa Fassi sat in the "Kiss and Cry" area waiting for her scores.
Then she beckoned Cousins to join them on the bench. As he put his arm around her, she buried her face in his shoulder and broke into tears again.
